questions.question: All birds can fly. Some birds cannot fly. Which of the following conclusions is correct?
questions.questionHtml:
All birds can fly.

Some birds cannot fly.

Which of the following conclusions is correct?
questions.solution:
Explanation: The two statements contradict each other:

“All birds can fly” is universal.

“Some birds cannot fly” negates it.

Since both cannot be true simultaneously, we accept the more specific and factual statement. Examples like ostriches and penguins confirm that some birds cannot fly , making that conclusion logically valid.

questions.question: All men are mortal. Socrates is a man. Which of the following is true?
questions.questionHtml:
All men are mortal.

Socrates is a man. Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
Explanation: This is a classic example of deductive reasoning:

Premise 1: All men are mortal.

Premise 2: Socrates is a man.

Conclusion: Therefore, Socrates is mortal .

This follows the logical structure: All A are B. C is A. Therefore, C is B.

questions.question: All flowers are plants. Some plants are flowering plants. Which conclusion is logically valid?
questions.questionHtml:
All flowers are plants.

Some plants are flowering plants. Which conclusion is logically valid?
questions.solution:
Statements:

All flowers are plants → Every flower is a type of plant.

Some plants are flowering plants → There exists a subset of plants that are flowering.

Now evaluate each option:

Some plants are flowers → ✅ Logically valid. Since all flowers are plants, it follows that some plants (those that are flowers) exist.

No plants are flowers → ❌ Contradicts statement 1.

Some flowers are not plants → ❌ Contradicts statement 1.

All plants are flowers → ❌ Overgeneralization. Only some plants are flowering.

✅ Correct answer: Some plants are flowers

questions.question: Which of the following conclusions can be logically drawn from the statement? "All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sour."
questions.questionHtml:
Which of the following conclusions can be logically drawn from the statement?
"All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sour."

options.text: Some fruits may not be apples.

questions.solution:
Statement: "All apples are fruits. Some fruits are sour."

✅ Conclusion 1: Some fruits may not be apples.

This logically follows .

Since all apples are fruits, but only some fruits are sour, it’s possible that there are fruits that are not apples . This is a valid possibility.

❌ Conclusion 2: All apples are sour.

This does not follow .

The statement says some fruits are sour, not that all fruits (including apples) are sour.

❌ Conclusion 3: Some apples are not fruits.

This directly contradicts the statement "All apples are fruits."

❌ Conclusion 4: All sour things are fruits.

This is an overgeneralization .

The statement only says some fruits are sour , not that all sour things must be fruits.

✅ Correct answer: Some fruits may not be apples.

questions.question: "All birds fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins fly." The flaw is:
questions.questionHtml: "All birds fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins fly." The flaw is:
questions.solution:
Statement : “All birds fly. Penguins are birds. Therefore, penguins fly.”

This seems logically valid if the premise is true. But in reality, not all birds fly — penguins are a clear exception.

So , the flaw lies in the first premise : “All birds fly” → This is factually incorrect .

Hence, the conclusion “penguins fly” is based on a false assumption , even though the reasoning is structurally valid.

✅ Correct answer: False premise

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows Statement: "People who regularly exercise are less likely to fall ill." Conclusions: I. Regular exercise improves immunity. II. Illness is directly linked to lack of physical activity.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows

Statement: "People who regularly exercise are less likely to fall ill."

Conclusions: I. Regular exercise improves immunity.

II. Illness is directly linked to lack of physical activity.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: The statement clearly indicates that people who exercise regularly are less likely to fall ill. This implies that exercise strengthens the body and enhances immunity, which supports Conclusion I. However, there is no direct mention in the statement that illness is caused solely due to lack of physical activity; such a link would be an assumption beyond the given information. Hence, only Conclusion I logically follows.

questions.question: Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume that the statements are absolutely true, even if they contradict common knowledge. Based only on the given information, determine which of the conclusions logically follow. Statements: All engineers are smart. Some smart people are creative. No creative person is dull. Conclusions: (1) Some smart people are not dull. (2) Some engineers are creative. (3) Some dull people are smart. (4) No engineer is dull.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume that the statements are absolutely true, even if they contradict common knowledge. Based only on the given information, determine which of the conclusions logically follow.

Statements:

All engineers are smart.

Some smart people are creative.

No creative person is dull.

Conclusions:

(1) Some smart people are not dull.

(2) Some engineers are creative.

(3) Some dull people are smart.

(4) No engineer is dull.
questions.solution:
(1) True, because some smart people are creative, and no creative is dull → so some smart are not dull.

(2) False, nothing is mentioned about engineers being creative.

(3) False, dull people cannot be smart as no creative is dull.

(4) False, not enough information to prove all engineers are not dull. Hence, only (1) follows.

(2) Some plants are not heavy. (3) Some flowers are heavy. (4) Some heavy things are not plants.

questions.solution:

questions.question: Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume the statements are absolutely true, even if they contradict commonly known facts. Based solely on the statements, determine which of the conclusions logically follow. Statements: All cars are vehicles. Some vehicles are bikes. No bike is a truck. Conclusions: (1) Some vehicles are not trucks. (2) No car is a bike. (3) Some cars are bikes. (4) Some trucks are vehicles.

questions.question: Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume the statements to be absolutely true, even if they contradict known facts. Based only on the information given in the statements, decide which of the conclusions logically follow. Statements: Some students are clever. All clever people are honest. No honest person is lazy. Conclusions: (1) Some students are honest. (2) No student is lazy. (3) Some clever people are not lazy. (4) Some honest people are not students.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume the statements to be absolutely true, even if they contradict known facts. Based only on the information given in the statements, decide which of the conclusions logically follow.

Statements:

Some students are clever.

All clever people are honest.

No honest person is lazy.

Conclusions:

(1) Some students are honest.

(2) No student is lazy.

(3) Some clever people are not lazy.

(4) Some honest people are not students.
questions.solution:
Analysis:
From (i) and (ii), some students are clever → hence some students are honest ⇒ Conclusion (1) follows .
From (ii) and (iii), clever → honest → not lazy ⇒ some clever people are not lazy ⇒ Conclusion (3) follows .
But we cannot say no student is lazy ⇒ (2) does not follow.
We also cannot confirm some honest people are not students ⇒ (4) does not follow.

Correct Answer: Only (1) and (3) follow.

questions.question: Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume the statements are absolutely true, even if they contradict commonly known facts. Based solely on the statements, determine which of the conclusions logically follows. Statements: Some birds are eagles. All eagles are fierce. All fierce creatures are predators. Conclusions: (1) Some birds are fierce. (2) Some birds are predators. (3) All predators are fierce. (4) No eagle is a predator.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Assume the statements are absolutely true, even if they contradict commonly known facts. Based solely on the statements, determine which of the conclusions logically follows.

Statements:

Some birds are eagles.

All eagles are fierce.

All fierce creatures are predators.

Conclusions:

(1) Some birds are fierce.

(2) Some birds are predators.

(3) All predators are fierce.

(4) No eagle is a predator.
questions.solution: From “Some birds are eagles” and “All eagles are fierce” ⇒ Some birds are fierce (1 follows). Since All fierce are predators , those birds are also predators ⇒ (2 follows). (3) does not follow because “All fierce are predators” does not imply the converse “All predators are fierce.” (4) is false because eagles ⊆ fierce ⊆ predators, so eagles are predators.

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: “Government should provide free education to all children up to the age of 14.” Conclusions: I. Education is a basic right of every child. II. A large number of children are deprived of basic education.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: “Government should provide free education to all children up to the age of 14.”

Conclusions:

I. Education is a basic right of every child.

II. A large number of children are deprived of basic education.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

questions.solution: Recommending free education up to 14 implies two underlying ideas: ( i ) the author treats education as a fundamental right for children (normative basis for the recommendation); and (ii) the recommendation addresses a problem that many children are currently deprived of basic education (reason for making it free). Hence both I and II follow .

questions.question: Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, disregarding commonly known facts. Use only the information provided. Statements: • All Dogs are Mammals. • All Mammals are Animals. • Some Animals are Pets. Conclusions: (1) All Dogs are Animals. (2) Some Mammals are Pets. (3) Some Dogs are Pets. (4) No Dog is a Pet.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statements and conclusions carefully. Decide which of the conclusions logically follow from the statements, disregarding commonly known facts. Use only the information provided.

Statements:

• All Dogs are Mammals.

• All Mammals are Animals.

• Some Animals are Pets.

Conclusions:

(1) All Dogs are Animals.

(2) Some Mammals are Pets.

(3) Some Dogs are Pets.

(4) No Dog is a Pet.
questions.solution: From the chain Dogs ⊆ Mammals ⊆ Animals , it follows that All Dogs are Animals ⇒ (1) follows. The statement “Some Animals are Pets” gives no information about Mammals or Dogs in that subset, so (2) and (3) do not follow. (4) also does not follow because nothing rules out dogs being pets. Hence, Only (1) follows .
